findings.summary: Underflow-guard condition on the audio-subtraction fallback is inverted.
findings.mechanism: The code takes `container_bps - audio_bps` only when `container_bps < audio_bps && audio_bps > 0`, i.e. exactly when the subtraction would underflow (container_bps is a u64, so this either panics in debug builds or wraps to a huge value in release). The valid case, `container_bps > audio_bps` (positive result), instead falls through to the `None =>` arm and uses the raw container total, meaning the new audio-subtraction fallback path this diff exists to add is never exercised. The comparison operator should be `>`, not `<`.

findings.summary: New video-only bitrate is computed but never used — the struct field is still populated from the old container-total variable.
findings.mechanism: `video_bitrate_mbps` (the new video-only estimate at line 277) is computed but `video_bitrate_mbps: total_bitrate_mbps` at line 340 still references the old identifier. Since `total_bitrate_mbps` was renamed/removed in this diff (replaced by `container_bps` as a raw u64, not an f32 mbps value), this either fails to compile, or if a stray `total_bitrate_mbps` binding still exists elsewhere, the struct is populated with the unmodified container total, defeating the entire purpose of the change (the video-only estimate is computed and silently discarded).
